# Adjudication Task — Chapter 178

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃178화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“객잔이 낡았군. 비가 새.”
  6|
  7|나는 애꿎은 천장만 바라봤다.
  8|
  9|“여기가 좀 낡긴 했죠.”
 10|
 11|물론 비는 내리지 않았고 먹빛 하늘은 잠잠했다.
 12|
 13|낡은 건 객잔이 아니라 적천강의 마음이다. 오래전의 아픈 추억을 떠올리니 그의 눈에서 비가 샌 것이다.
 14|
 15|‘피도 눈물도 없는 노인네인 줄 알았는데.’
 16|
 17|화왕 적천강.
 18|
 19|저 괴팍한 성격의 초절정 고수에게 이런 과거가 있을 줄은 몰랐다. 그저 미친놈이라고 생각했던 조필에 대해서도 평가를 수정해야 했다.
 20|
 21|‘상상 이상으로 미친놈이었네.’
 22|
 23|죽을 뻔한 자신을 구해 준 사부를 철저히 이용하고 버렸다. 이야기를 들어 보면 마지막까지 한 줌의 죄책감도 없었음이 분명했다.
 24|
 25|나는 이 정도로 순수한 악의(惡意)에 가득 찬 놈이 있다는 사실에 놀랐고, 조필이 더 이상 이 세상에 존재하지 않는다는 사실에 안도했다.
 26|
 27|“그런데 용케 살아서 도망쳤군요. 남궁세가 쪽에서도 예의주시하고 있었을 텐데.”
 28|
 29|남궁세가, 무협 소설의 단골손님.
 30|
 31|무려 구파일방과 비견된다는 천하오대세가에 속해 있는 남궁세가다. 모르긴 몰라도 도망자 한 명 잡아 죽이는 것쯤은 일도 아니었을 것이다.
 32|
 33|누군가의 도움이 있지 않고서야.
 34|
 35|“혹시?”
 36|
 37|내 물음에 적천강이 담담하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 38|
 39|“창천검왕을 찾아가 부탁했지. 그것이 내 마지막 도리였다.”
 40|
 41|제자는 사부를 버리고 떠났지만 사부는 그런 제자를 끝까지 지켰다.
 42|
 43|정말이지 들을수록 기가 찬 사제지간이 아닐 수 없다.
 44|
 45|“……대단하시네요.”
 46|
 47|“대단? 녀석 같은 살성을 제자로 키운 것으로도 모자라 사사로운 정에 사로잡혀 세상에 풀어놓은 내가? 그건 어리석은 선택이었다.”
 48|
 49|적천강이 자조 섞인 웃음과 함께 말을 이었다.
 50|
 51|“창천검왕도 내게 그러더군. 후회할 거라고. 그 말이 맞았다. 지난 십 년의 세월, 매 순간순간이 후회였다.”
 52|
 53|“만약 그날로 돌아간다면 어떻게 하시겠습니까?”
 54|
 55|대답에는 망설임이 없었다.
 56|
 57|“살릴 것이다. 그리고 다시 후회하겠지. 백 번의 기회가 있다 하더라도 그때의 나는 그랬을 것이다.”
 58|
 59|‘그때의 나’는 그랬을 거라고?
 60|
 61|의미심장하게 들리는 한마디였다. 지금의 적천강은 다르다는 뜻이기도 하니까.
 62|
 63|‘혹시?’
 64|
 65|어쩌면 십 년이라는 세월은 그 나름대로 준비를 위한 시간이었을지도 모른다는 생각이 들었다.
 66|
 67|지금도 세상 어디에선가 악행을 저지를 제자를 직접 죽이기 위한 마음의 준비 말이다.
 68|
 69|‘만약 그렇다면…….’
 70|
 71|문득 뇌리를 스치는 생각에 나는 조심스럽게, 아주 조심스럽게 물었다.
 72|
 73|“저기.”
 74|
 75|“말해 보거라.”
 76|
 77|적천강의 가라앉은 목소리. 모든 것을 꿰뚫어 보는 듯한 심유한 눈빛에 심장이 요동친다.
 78|
 79|나는 마른침을 삼킨 뒤 입을 뗐다.
 80|
 81|“제게 묻고 싶으신 것이 있는 걸로 압니다.”
 82|
 83|애초에 이렇게 마주 보고 있는 것은 옛 기억을 회상하기 위해서가 아니다.
 84|
 85|그는 나에게, 나는 그에게.
 86|
 87|우리는 서로에게 묻고 답할 것이 있었다. 그리고 칼자루를 쥐고 있는 것은 내가 아니다.
 88|
 89|“대답해 드리겠습니다. 뭐든지.”
 90|
 91|“…….”
 92|
 93|칼자루를 쥔 자, 적천강은 말없이 텅 빈 술잔을 매만졌다.
 94|
 95|그건 끝이 정해지지 않은 침묵이었다. 일각? 한 식경? 아니면 반 시진? 시간이 얼마나 흘렀는지 알 수 없었다.
 96|
 97|밖에는 찬 바람이 쌩쌩 부는데, 긴장감 때문인지 전신이 땀으로 흠뻑 젖었다.
 98|
 99|그리고 마침내 긴 침묵이 깨졌다.
100|
101|“……죽었느냐?”
102|
103|잔뜩 쉰 목소리. 담담한 척 애써 보지만 여러 감정이 뒤섞인 물음이다.
104|
105|내가 고개를 끄덕이자 노인의 회색 눈동자가 파르르 떨렸다.
106|
107|“그랬군. 결국, 그렇게 됐어.”
108|
109|무심코 술잔을 기울이려던 적천강이 이내 술잔이 비어 있다는 사실을 알아채고 허탈하게 웃었다.
110|
111|“어느 정도는 짐작하고 있었다. 네 녀석에게서 본문의 흔적을 느꼈으니까.”
112|
113|열화신단으로 얻은 공력 때문이다. 내가 적천강의 공력을 통해 그가 화왕임을 짐작했듯이 그도 마찬가지였다.
114|
115|“편안하게 갔느냐?”
116|
117|“그건.”
118|
119|칠공에서 피를 흘리며 발악하던 조필의 모습이 떠올랐다.
120|
121|선천지기까지 끌어 올린 놈은 나와의 사투 끝에 상반신의 절반이 날아가 죽었다.
122|
123|내가 대답을 주저하자 적천강이 주름진 손을 내저었다.
124|
125|“되었다. 괜한 것을 물은 내 잘못이다. 무인들의 싸움에 편안한 죽음이 어디 있을까.”
126|
127|“고통은 짧았을 겁니다.”
128|
129|“한평생 수많은 이들에게 고통만 주던 녀석이니, 그 정도면 분수에 넘치는 죽음이지.”
130|
131|말과는 달리 씁쓸한 얼굴이었다.
132|
133|만약 적천강이 조필을 만났더라면 그는 자신이 할 수 있는 최선의 한 수를 펼쳤을 것이다.
134|
135|가장 빠르고, 고통 없는 죽음을 내렸을 테다.
136|
137|‘어쩌면 그걸 위해 다시 세상에 나왔을지도 모르지.’
138|
139|하지만 적천강의 목적은 이뤄지지 못했다. 조필은 옛 스승보다 한발 빨리 나를 만났고, 목숨을 잃었다.
140|
141|과연 적천강이 어떻게 반응할…….
142|
143|“빚을 졌구나.”
144|
145|“예?”
146|
147|“못 들었느냐? 네게 빚을 졌다고 했다.”
148|
149|“아뇨, 듣긴 했는데.”
150|
151|얼떨떨해서 그러지.
152|
153|이렇게 쉽게, 간단하게 저런 말이 나올 줄은 정말 꿈에도 몰랐다.
154|
155|이게 무슨 일인가 싶어 눈을 깜빡이는 내게 적천강이 말했다.
156|
157|“누군가는 그 아이를 멈춰야 했다. 십 년 전 내가 했어야 할 일을 네가 대신한 것이다. 그리고…….”
158|
159|돌연 적천강이 입술을 움찔거렸다. 마치 누군가에게 그런 말을 하는 것이 처음인 사람처럼.
160|
161|잠깐 주춤하던 그가 마침내 입을 뗐다.
162|
163|“미안하다. 일전의 섣부른 행동에 대해서 너희들 전부에게 진심으로 사과하마.”
164|
165|나도 모르게 목소리가 튀어나왔다.
166|
167|“헐.”
168|
169|“헐?”
170|
171|“아, 아닙니다. 너무 놀라서 저도 모르게 그만.”
172|
173|“노부가 사과하는 것이 그렇게 놀랄 일이냐?”
174|
175|충분히 그럴 만한 일인 것 같은데. 그리고 본인도 엄청 어색해했으면서, 뭘.
176|
177|“……어, 그게.”
178|
179|어물쩍 말꼬리를 흐리던 나는 일그러지는 적천강의 얼굴을 보고 얼른 말을 바꿨다.
180|
181|“천하에 명성이 자자하신 화왕 적천강 대협께서 저같이 한참 어린 후배에게 직접 사과까지 하시다니! 적 대협의 호쾌한 성품과 겸손함에 저절로 허리가 굽혀질 뿐입니다.”
182|
183|“…….”
184|
185|“…….”
186|
187|얼굴 표정 봐라. 지킬과 하이드의 싸움이 따로 없다.
188|
189|나를 때릴지 말지, 극심한 내면 갈등을 얼굴 근육으로 표현하던 적천강이 이내 한숨을 내쉬었다.
190|
191|“도무지 종잡을 수 없는 놈이군. 이만 물러가거라.”
192|
193|“넵.”
194|
195|“저 아이들도 모두 데려가고.”
196|
197|청풍은 탁자에 이마를 박고 쿨쿨 자는 중이고 혁무진은 여전히 마당에 엎어져 있다.
198|
199|적천강의 마음이 바뀌기 전에 잽싸게 짐덩이들을 수거한 뒤 2층으로 올라가려는데 잊고 있던 사실 하나가 떠올랐다.
200|
201|‘아, 맞다. 화염신장의 비급이랑 검은 돌려줘야 하는데.’
202|
203|열화신단은 이미 먹어 버렸으니 어쩔 수 없다지만 남은 물건들은 돌려줘야 한다.
204|
205|적천광과의 문제는 오늘 하루를 마지막으로 끝내고 싶은 마음이 간절했다.
206|
207|“저어, 적 대협. 죄송하지만 하나 더 말씀드릴 것이……”
208|
209|개미만 한 목소리와 함께 돌아선 나는 다음 순간, 곧장 멈칫했다.
210|
211|쪼르르륵.
212|
213|홀로 남겨진 적천강이 술을 따르고 있었다.
214|
215|한 잔, 그리고 두 잔. 텅 빈 맞은편 자리에 술잔을 내려놓은 그가 말없이 술을 마시기 시작했다.
216|
217|물끄러미 그 모습을 바라보다가 문득 생각했다.
218|
219|‘작네.’
220|
221|화왕(火王)이라 불리는 거인의 뒷모습은 작고 쓸쓸했고, 나는 조용히 돌아서서 계단을 올랐다.
222|
223|
224|
225|* * *
226|
227|
228|
229|등 뒤의 기척이 사라지고, 적천강이 중얼거렸다.
230|
231|“넌 죽어 마땅한 놈이다.”
232|
233|안휘성에서만 수십을 죽였다. 지난 십 년간 얼마나 많은 이들이 제자의 손에 희생되었을지 짐작도 되지 않았다.
234|
235|“강자 지존이라 했더냐. 너도 마찬가지다. 결국 너보다 강한 자의 손에 죽은 게야.”
236|
237|영원한 강자도, 약자도 없다.
238|
239|초절정 고수인 적천강도 결국 누군가에게는 약자다.
240|
241|그러나 종종 그 사실을 착각하는 자들이 있다. 스스로의 힘에 취해서, 또는 피에 취해서 잘못된 길에 들어선다.
242|
243|“한심한 놈 같으니.”
244|
245|적천강은 술을 들이켰다. 오래전 그날, 제자가 했던 말이 귓가에 메아리치는 듯했다.
246|
247|
248|
249|‘저는 변한 적이 없습니다. 사부님을 처음 만난 그날부터 지금까지 단 한 번도.’
250|
251|
252|
253|지난 십 년간 수도 없이 곱씹었던 말이다. 저 한마디가 심장 어림에 비수처럼 박혀 그를 괴롭게 만들었다.
254|
255|“정녕 변하지 않았단 말이냐, 단 한 번도?”
256|
257|오랜 시간을 함께했다. 때로는 엄한 스승이었고, 자상한 아버지처럼 제자를 돌봤다.
258|
259|아니, 그렇다고 믿었다.
260|
261|하지만 그 모든 것이 전부 착각이었다. 진정 그랬다면 장천이 택한 길은 지금과는 많이 달라졌을 것이다.
262|
263|“처음부터 검은 화선지가 어디 있으랴.”
264|
265|세상에 나온다는 것은 한 장의 화선지를 받는 것과 같다.
266|
267|사람이 태어나고 죽기까지 거치는 수많은 순간.
268|
269|마침내 죽음이 찾아오면 그 순간들로 채워진 한 폭의 그림이 완성된다. 장천이 그려 낸 그림은…… 온통 먹빛이다.
270|
271|적천강은 가장 가까이서 그것을 지켜보면서도 알지 못했다.
272|
273|“천아.”
274|
275|노인은 술잔이 놓인 맞은편 자리를 응시했다. 아무도 앉지 않은 그곳에 환영 같은 모습들이 차례차례 떠오른다.
276|
277|잔뜩 웅크린 채 만두를 욱여넣던 아이, 사부가 만들어 준 목검을 쥐고 뺨을 발갛게 붉힌 소년.
278|
279|점점 팔다리가 길어지고 눈빛은 날카로워진다. 어느새 훌쩍 큰 청년이 노인을 노려보고 있었다.
280|
281|
282|
283|‘죽이십시오.’
284|
285|
286|
287|그날, 적천강은 제자의 날 선 말에 아무런 대답도 하지 못했다.
288|
289|그러나 다시 제자를 만나게 된다면 반드시 해 주고픈 말이 있었다.
290|
291|“미안하구나. 미안해.”
292|
293|휘이이잉.
294|
295|낡은 객잔의 문 사이로 흘러들어 온 찬 바람이 술잔 위를 스쳤다.
296|
297|
298|
299|* * *
300|
301|
302|
303|“은인!”
304|
305|요란한 소리에 눈을 떴다. 어쩐지 잔뜩 신이 난 청풍이 방방 뛰고 있었다.
306|
307|“여긴 내 전각인데 왜…… 아.”
308|
309|맞다. 여긴 태원 진가가 아니라 객잔이었지.
310|
311|동시에 어제 일이 파노라마처럼 머릿속을 스친다. 삶과 죽음의 경계를 넘었다고 해도 과언이 아니다.
312|
313|뭐 그건 그렇고.
314|
315|“그만 좀 뛰어요. 가뜩이나 먼지도 많은데.”
316|
317|“오늘은 뛰어도 돼요!”

It seemed plenty astonishing to me. Besides, he’d looked incredibly uncomfortable saying it, so what was he complaining about?

[P88]
“…Well, you see…”

[P89]
I trailed off awkwardly, then saw Jeok Cheongang’s face beginning to contort and quickly changed my tune.

[P90]
“The renowned Fire King, Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, personally apologizing to a junior as young as me! I can only bow before your magnanimity and humility.”

[P91]
“…”

[P92]
“…”

[P93]
Just look at his face. Jekyll and Hyde were fighting it out right there.

[P94]
Every muscle in Jeok Cheongang’s face conveyed his fierce inner struggle over whether or not to hit me. Eventually, he sighed.

[P95]
“I cannot make heads or tails of you. You may leave now.”

[P96]
“Yes, sir.”

[P97]
“And take those children with you.”

[P98]
Cheongpung was fast asleep with his forehead pressed against the table, while Hyuk Mujin was still sprawled facedown in the courtyard.

[P99]
Before Jeok Cheongang could change his mind, I quickly gathered up the two deadweights and headed for the second floor. Then I remembered something.

[P100]
*Oh, right. I have to return the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual and the sword.*

[P101]
I had already swallowed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, so there was nothing I could do about that, but I still needed to return the other items.

[P102]
I desperately wanted to settle everything between Jeok Cheongang and me once and for all today.

[P103]
“Um, Sir Jeok. I’m sorry, but there’s one more thing I need to tell you…”

[P104]
I turned back, my voice as tiny as an ant, then stopped short.

[P105]
Wine trickled into a glass.

[P106]
Left alone, Jeok Cheongang was pouring drinks.

[P107]
One glass, then another. He placed the second wineglass before the empty seat across from him and began drinking in silence.

[P108]
I watched him for a moment, then suddenly thought:

[P109]
*He looks small.*

[P110]
The back of the giant known as the Fire King looked small and lonely.

[P111]
I quietly turned away and climbed the stairs.

[P112]
* * *

[P113]
Once the presence behind him had disappeared, Jeok Cheongang muttered,

[P114]
“You deserved to die.”

[P115]
Jangcheon had killed dozens in Anhui alone. There was no telling how many people had fallen victim to his Disciple over the past ten years.

[P116]
“‘Might makes right,’ was it? The same applied to you. In the end, you died at the hands of someone stronger.”

[P117]
No one remained strong forever, just as no one remained weak forever.

[P118]
Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, was weaker than someone.

[P119]
Yet some people forgot that fact. Drunk on their own strength—or on blood—they strayed down the wrong path.

[P120]
“What a pathetic fool.”

[P121]
Jeok Cheongang drained his drink. His Disciple’s words from that day long ago seemed to echo in his ears.

[P122]
*I have never changed. Not once, from the day I first met you until now.*

[P123]
Over the past ten years, he had turned those words over in his mind countless times. That single sentence had lodged near his heart like a dagger and tormented him.

[P124]
“Did you truly never change? Not even once?”

[P125]
They had spent many years together. At times, Jeok Cheongang had been a strict teacher; at others, he had cared for his Disciple like a loving father.

[P126]
No—he had believed that was what he had done.

[P127]
But it had all been an illusion. If it had truly been otherwise, Jangcheon would have chosen a very different path.

[P128]
“How could rice paper be black from the beginning?”

[P129]
Being born into this world was like receiving a blank sheet of rice paper.

[P130]
A person passed through countless moments between birth and death.

[P131]
When death finally arrived, those moments came together to complete a single painting. The painting Jangcheon had created was… entirely ink-black.

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang had watched from closer than anyone, yet he had never seen it.

[P133]
“Cheon.”

[P134]
The old man stared at the seat across from him, where a wineglass had been set. One by one, phantomlike figures appeared in the empty chair.

[P135]
A child hunched over as he stuffed dumplings into his mouth. A boy clutching the wooden sword his Master had made for him, his cheeks flushed bright red.

[P136]
His limbs lengthened, and his gaze sharpened. Before long, a tall young man stood glaring at the old man.

[P137]
*Kill me.*

[P138]
That day, Jeok Cheongang had been unable to answer his Disciple’s cutting words.

[P139]
But if he ever met his Disciple again, there was something he had desperately wanted to say.

[P140]
“I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.”

[P141]
A cold wind whistled through the door of the old inn and swept across the wineglass.

[P142]
* * *

[P143]
“Benefactor!”

[P144]
I awoke to a terrible racket. Cheongpung, practically bursting with excitement, was bouncing up and down.

[P145]
“This is my pavilion, so why are you… Ah.”

[P146]
Right. This wasn’t the Jin Family of Taiyuan. It was an inn.

[P147]
At the same time, the events of the previous day flashed through my mind like a panorama. It wouldn’t have been an exaggeration to say I had crossed the boundary between life and death.

[P148]
Well, that aside—

[P149]
“Stop jumping around. There’s enough dust in here already.”

[P150]
“I’m allowed to jump today!”

[P151]
How was anyone supposed to sleep through this?

[P152]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been curled up like a shrimp in one corner of the floor, blearily opened his eyes.

[P153]
“Is this… paradise?”

[P154]
That bastard started talking nonsense the moment he woke up.

[P155]
It was absurd, but then I remembered that yesterday, after trying to escape on his own, he had been knocked unconscious by a duck bone Jeok Cheongang flicked at him.

[P156]
“You awake?”

[P157]
“Captain?”

[P158]
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened when he saw me. Then he sighed.

[P159]
“So this isn’t paradise.”

[P160]
“…What the hell is that supposed to mean, you bastard?”

[P161]
“It was a joke. A joke. I’m just glad to see you alive again.”

[P162]
“Says the guy who tried to run away on his own.”

[P163]
“Come on. Why do you have to put it like that?”

[P164]
Grinning shamelessly, Hyuk Mujin looked around. More precisely, he looked at Cheongpung, who was running laps around the room like a train.

[P165]
“What’s all this commotion so early in the morning? What happened to make him run around like that?”

[P166]
“No idea. He says he’s allowed to jump today.”

[P167]
“He must’ve eaten something tasty.”

[P168]
“…”

[P169]
It was obviously bullshit, but since we were talking about Cheongpung, its credibility skyrocketed.

[P170]
Giving him a doubtful look, I asked Cheongpung,

[P171]
“What day is it today?”

[P172]
Cheongpung, who had been circling the room and driving me crazy, stopped dead.

[P173]
“Benefactor, you don’t even know that?”

[P174]
“…Let’s refrain from saying things like that. It hits ten times harder coming from you.”

[P175]
“It’s the first day of the new year. New Year’s Day!”

[P176]
Hyuk Mujin and I nodded at the same time.

[P177]
“Ah, so it’s New Year’s Day.”

[P178]
“Right. It’s already New Year’s Day.”

[P179]
“I thought it was something els—”

[P180]
“Yeah. A whole year has already pass—”

[P181]
After a brief silence, a profound realization struck us.

[P182]
*Ah. The Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

[P183]
At that moment, Wipeng’s threat from before I left the family rang vividly in my ears.

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

“I see. So that’s how it ended.”

[P54]
Jeok Cheongang started to tip back his wineglass out of habit, then realized it was empty and gave a hollow laugh.

[P55]
“I suspected as much. I sensed traces of our sect in you.”

[P56]
It was because of the internal energy I had gained from the Blazing Flame Divine Pill. Just as his internal energy had led me to suspect that he was the Fire King, mine had told him the same thing.

[P57]
“Did he die peacefully?”

[P58]
“That…”

[P59]
I pictured Jopil thrashing as blood streamed from his seven apertures.

[P60]
After drawing on even his innate qi, he had fought me to the death and died with half his upper body blown away.

[P61]
When I hesitated, Jeok Cheongang waved a wrinkled hand.

[P62]
“Enough. It was my fault for asking a pointless question. What peaceful death is there in a battle between martial artists?”

[P63]
“His suffering would have been brief.”

[P64]
“A man who spent his life inflicting pain on countless others received a better death than he deserved.”

[P65]
Despite his words, his expression was bitter.

[P66]
If Jeok Cheongang had found Jopil, he would have used the finest move at his disposal.

[P67]
He would have granted him the swiftest, most painless death possible.

[P68]
*Maybe that was why he returned to the world.*

[P69]
But Jeok Cheongang had failed to achieve his goal. Jopil had encountered me before his former Master could reach him, and lost his life.

[P70]
How would Jeok Cheongang react—

[P71]
“I owe you a debt.”

[P72]
“Pardon?”

[P73]
“Did you not hear me? I said I owe you.”

[P74]
“No, I heard you. It’s just…”

[P75]
I was dumbfounded.

[P76]
Never in my wildest dreams had I expected those words to come from him so easily.

[P77]
As I blinked at him, wondering what on earth was happening, Jeok Cheongang continued.

[P78]
“Someone had to stop that child. You did in my stead what I should have done ten years ago. And…”

[P79]
Jeok Cheongang’s lips suddenly twitched, as though he had never said anything like this to anyone before.

[P80]
After a brief hesitation, he finally spoke.

[P81]
“I’m sorry. I sincerely apologize to all of you for acting so rashly before.”

[P82]
The word slipped out before I could stop it.

[P83]
“Whoa.”

[P84]
“Whoa?”

[P85]
“Ah, it’s nothing. I was so surprised that it just slipped out.”

[P86]
“Is it truly so astonishing for this old man to apologize?”

[P87]
It seemed plenty astonishing to me. Besides, he’d looked incredibly uncomfortable saying it, so what was he complaining about?

[P88]
“…Well, you see…”

[P89]
I trailed off awkwardly, then saw Jeok Cheongang’s face beginning to contort and quickly changed my tune.

[P90]
“The renowned Fire King, Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, personally apologizing to a junior as young as me! I can only bow before your magnanimity and humility.”

[P91]
“…”

[P92]
“…”

[P93]
Just look at his face. Jekyll and Hyde were fighting it out right there.

[P94]
Every muscle in Jeok Cheongang’s face conveyed his fierce inner struggle over whether or not to hit me. Eventually, he sighed.

[P95]
“I cannot make heads or tails of you. You may leave now.”

[P96]
“Yes, sir.”

[P97]
“And take those children with you.”

[P98]
Cheongpung was fast asleep with his forehead pressed against the table, while Hyuk Mujin was still sprawled facedown in the courtyard.

[P99]
Before Jeok Cheongang could change his mind, I quickly gathered up the two deadweights and headed for the second floor. Then I remembered something.

[P100]
*Oh, right. I have to return the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual and the sword.*

[P101]
I had already swallowed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, so there was nothing I could do about that, but I still needed to return the other items.

[P102]
I desperately wanted to settle everything between Jeok Cheongang and me once and for all today.

[P103]
“Um, Sir Jeok. I’m sorry, but there’s one more thing I need to tell you…”

[P104]
I turned back, my voice as tiny as an ant, then stopped short.

[P105]
Wine trickled into a glass.

[P106]
Left alone, Jeok Cheongang was pouring drinks.

[P107]
One glass, then another. He placed the second wineglass before the empty seat across from him and began drinking in silence.

[P108]
I watched him for a moment, then suddenly thought:

[P109]
*He looks small.*

[P110]
The back of the giant known as the Fire King looked small and lonely.

[P111]
I quietly turned away and climbed the stairs.

[P112]
* * *

[P113]
Once the presence behind him had disappeared, Jeok Cheongang muttered,

[P114]
“You deserved to die.”

[P115]
Jangcheon had killed dozens in Anhui alone. There was no telling how many people had fallen victim to his Disciple over the past ten years.

[P116]
“‘Might makes right,’ was it? The same applied to you. In the end, you died at the hands of someone stronger.”

[P117]
No one remained strong forever, just as no one remained weak forever.

[P118]
Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, was weaker than someone.

[P119]
Yet some people forgot that fact. Drunk on their own strength—or on blood—they strayed down the wrong path.

[P120]
“What a pathetic fool.”

[P121]
Jeok Cheongang drained his drink. His Disciple’s words from that day long ago seemed to echo in his ears.

[P122]
*I have never changed. Not once, from the day I first met you until now.*

[P123]
Over the past ten years, he had turned those words over in his mind countless times. That single sentence had lodged near his heart like a dagger and tormented him.

[P124]
“Did you truly never change? Not even once?”

[P125]
They had spent many years together. At times, Jeok Cheongang had been a strict teacher; at others, he had cared for his Disciple like a loving father.

[P126]
No—he had believed that was what he had done.

[P127]
But it had all been an illusion. If it had truly been otherwise, Jangcheon would have chosen a very different path.

[P128]
“How could rice paper be black from the beginning?”

[P129]
Being born into this world was like receiving a blank sheet of rice paper.

[P130]
A person passed through countless moments between birth and death.

[P131]
When death finally arrived, those moments came together to complete a single painting. The painting Jangcheon had created was… entirely ink-black.

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang had watched from closer than anyone, yet he had never seen it.

[P133]
“Cheon.”

[P134]
The old man stared at the seat across from him, where a wineglass had been set. One by one, phantomlike figures appeared in the empty chair.

[P135]
A child hunched over as he stuffed dumplings into his mouth. A boy clutching the wooden sword his Master had made for him, his cheeks flushed bright red.

[P136]
His limbs lengthened, and his gaze sharpened. Before long, a tall young man stood glaring at the old man.

[P137]
*Kill me.*

[P138]
That day, Jeok Cheongang had been unable to answer his Disciple’s cutting words.

[P139]
But if he ever met his Disciple again, there was something he had desperately wanted to say.

[P140]
“I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.”

[P141]
A cold wind whistled through the door of the old inn and swept across the wineglass.

[P142]
* * *

[P143]
“Benefactor!”

[P144]
I awoke to a terrible racket. Cheongpung, practically bursting with excitement, was bouncing up and down.

[P145]
“This is my pavilion, so why are you… Ah.”

[P146]
Right. This wasn’t the Jin Family of Taiyuan. It was an inn.

[P147]
At the same time, the events of the previous day flashed through my mind like a panorama. It wouldn’t have been an exaggeration to say I had crossed the boundary between life and death.

[P148]
Well, that aside—

[P149]
“Stop jumping around. There’s enough dust in here already.”

[P150]
“I’m allowed to jump today!”

[P151]
How was anyone supposed to sleep through this?

[P152]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been curled up like a shrimp in one corner of the floor, blearily opened his eyes.

[P153]
“Is this… paradise?”

[P154]
That bastard started talking nonsense the moment he woke up.

[P155]
It was absurd, but then I remembered that yesterday, after trying to escape on his own, he had been knocked unconscious by a duck bone Jeok Cheongang flicked at him.

[P156]
“You awake?”

[P157]
“Captain?”

[P158]
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened when he saw me. Then he sighed.

[P159]
“So this isn’t paradise.”

[P160]
“…What the hell is that supposed to mean, you bastard?”

[P161]
“It was a joke. A joke. I’m just glad to see you alive again.”

[P162]
“Says the guy who tried to run away on his own.”

[P163]
“Come on. Why do you have to put it like that?”

[P164]
Grinning shamelessly, Hyuk Mujin looked around. More precisely, he looked at Cheongpung, who was running laps around the room like a train.

[P165]
“What’s all this commotion so early in the morning? What happened to make him run around like that?”

[P166]
“No idea. He says he’s allowed to jump today.”

[P167]
“He must’ve eaten something tasty.”

[P168]
“…”

[P169]
It was obviously bullshit, but since we were talking about Cheongpung, its credibility skyrocketed.

[P170]
Giving him a doubtful look, I asked Cheongpung,

[P171]
“What day is it today?”

[P172]
Cheongpung, who had been circling the room and driving me crazy, stopped dead.

[P173]
“Benefactor, you don’t even know that?”

[P174]
“…Let’s refrain from saying things like that. It hits ten times harder coming from you.”

[P175]
“It’s the first day of the new year. New Year’s Day!”

[P176]
Hyuk Mujin and I nodded at the same time.

[P177]
“Ah, so it’s New Year’s Day.”

[P178]
“Right. It’s already New Year’s Day.”

[P179]
“I thought it was something els—”

[P180]
“Yeah. A whole year has already pass—”

[P181]
After a brief silence, a profound realization struck us.

[P182]
*Ah. The Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

[P183]
At that moment, Wipeng’s threat from before I left the family rang vividly in my ears.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 178

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃178화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“객잔이 낡았군. 비가 새.”
  6|
  7|나는 애꿎은 천장만 바라봤다.
  8|
  9|“여기가 좀 낡긴 했죠.”
 10|
 11|물론 비는 내리지 않았고 먹빛 하늘은 잠잠했다.
 12|
 13|낡은 건 객잔이 아니라 적천강의 마음이다. 오래전의 아픈 추억을 떠올리니 그의 눈에서 비가 샌 것이다.
 14|
 15|‘피도 눈물도 없는 노인네인 줄 알았는데.’
 16|
 17|화왕 적천강.
 18|
 19|저 괴팍한 성격의 초절정 고수에게 이런 과거가 있을 줄은 몰랐다. 그저 미친놈이라고 생각했던 조필에 대해서도 평가를 수정해야 했다.
 20|
 21|‘상상 이상으로 미친놈이었네.’
 22|
 23|죽을 뻔한 자신을 구해 준 사부를 철저히 이용하고 버렸다. 이야기를 들어 보면 마지막까지 한 줌의 죄책감도 없었음이 분명했다.
 24|
 25|나는 이 정도로 순수한 악의(惡意)에 가득 찬 놈이 있다는 사실에 놀랐고, 조필이 더 이상 이 세상에 존재하지 않는다는 사실에 안도했다.
 26|
 27|“그런데 용케 살아서 도망쳤군요. 남궁세가 쪽에서도 예의주시하고 있었을 텐데.”
 28|
 29|남궁세가, 무협 소설의 단골손님.
 30|
 31|무려 구파일방과 비견된다는 천하오대세가에 속해 있는 남궁세가다. 모르긴 몰라도 도망자 한 명 잡아 죽이는 것쯤은 일도 아니었을 것이다.
 32|
 33|누군가의 도움이 있지 않고서야.
 34|
 35|“혹시?”
 36|
 37|내 물음에 적천강이 담담하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 38|
 39|“창천검왕을 찾아가 부탁했지. 그것이 내 마지막 도리였다.”
 40|
 41|제자는 사부를 버리고 떠났지만 사부는 그런 제자를 끝까지 지켰다.
 42|
 43|정말이지 들을수록 기가 찬 사제지간이 아닐 수 없다.
 44|
 45|“……대단하시네요.”
 46|
 47|“대단? 녀석 같은 살성을 제자로 키운 것으로도 모자라 사사로운 정에 사로잡혀 세상에 풀어놓은 내가? 그건 어리석은 선택이었다.”
 48|
 49|적천강이 자조 섞인 웃음과 함께 말을 이었다.
 50|
 51|“창천검왕도 내게 그러더군. 후회할 거라고. 그 말이 맞았다. 지난 십 년의 세월, 매 순간순간이 후회였다.”
 52|
 53|“만약 그날로 돌아간다면 어떻게 하시겠습니까?”
 54|
 55|대답에는 망설임이 없었다.
 56|
 57|“살릴 것이다. 그리고 다시 후회하겠지. 백 번의 기회가 있다 하더라도 그때의 나는 그랬을 것이다.”
 58|
 59|‘그때의 나’는 그랬을 거라고?
 60|
 61|의미심장하게 들리는 한마디였다. 지금의 적천강은 다르다는 뜻이기도 하니까.
 62|
 63|‘혹시?’
 64|
 65|어쩌면 십 년이라는 세월은 그 나름대로 준비를 위한 시간이었을지도 모른다는 생각이 들었다.
 66|
 67|지금도 세상 어디에선가 악행을 저지를 제자를 직접 죽이기 위한 마음의 준비 말이다.
 68|
 69|‘만약 그렇다면…….’
 70|
 71|문득 뇌리를 스치는 생각에 나는 조심스럽게, 아주 조심스럽게 물었다.
 72|
 73|“저기.”
 74|
 75|“말해 보거라.”
 76|
 77|적천강의 가라앉은 목소리. 모든 것을 꿰뚫어 보는 듯한 심유한 눈빛에 심장이 요동친다.
 78|
 79|나는 마른침을 삼킨 뒤 입을 뗐다.
 80|
 81|“제게 묻고 싶으신 것이 있는 걸로 압니다.”
 82|
 83|애초에 이렇게 마주 보고 있는 것은 옛 기억을 회상하기 위해서가 아니다.
 84|
 85|그는 나에게, 나는 그에게.
 86|
 87|우리는 서로에게 묻고 답할 것이 있었다. 그리고 칼자루를 쥐고 있는 것은 내가 아니다.
 88|
 89|“대답해 드리겠습니다. 뭐든지.”
 90|
 91|“…….”
 92|
 93|칼자루를 쥔 자, 적천강은 말없이 텅 빈 술잔을 매만졌다.
 94|
 95|그건 끝이 정해지지 않은 침묵이었다. 일각? 한 식경? 아니면 반 시진? 시간이 얼마나 흘렀는지 알 수 없었다.
 96|
 97|밖에는 찬 바람이 쌩쌩 부는데, 긴장감 때문인지 전신이 땀으로 흠뻑 젖었다.
 98|
 99|그리고 마침내 긴 침묵이 깨졌다.
100|
101|“……죽었느냐?”
102|
103|잔뜩 쉰 목소리. 담담한 척 애써 보지만 여러 감정이 뒤섞인 물음이다.
104|
105|내가 고개를 끄덕이자 노인의 회색 눈동자가 파르르 떨렸다.
106|
107|“그랬군. 결국, 그렇게 됐어.”
108|
109|무심코 술잔을 기울이려던 적천강이 이내 술잔이 비어 있다는 사실을 알아채고 허탈하게 웃었다.
110|
111|“어느 정도는 짐작하고 있었다. 네 녀석에게서 본문의 흔적을 느꼈으니까.”
112|
113|열화신단으로 얻은 공력 때문이다. 내가 적천강의 공력을 통해 그가 화왕임을 짐작했듯이 그도 마찬가지였다.
114|
115|“편안하게 갔느냐?”
116|
117|“그건.”
118|
119|칠공에서 피를 흘리며 발악하던 조필의 모습이 떠올랐다.
120|
121|선천지기까지 끌어 올린 놈은 나와의 사투 끝에 상반신의 절반이 날아가 죽었다.
122|
123|내가 대답을 주저하자 적천강이 주름진 손을 내저었다.
124|
125|“되었다. 괜한 것을 물은 내 잘못이다. 무인들의 싸움에 편안한 죽음이 어디 있을까.”
126|
127|“고통은 짧았을 겁니다.”
128|
129|“한평생 수많은 이들에게 고통만 주던 녀석이니, 그 정도면 분수에 넘치는 죽음이지.”
130|
131|말과는 달리 씁쓸한 얼굴이었다.
132|
133|만약 적천강이 조필을 만났더라면 그는 자신이 할 수 있는 최선의 한 수를 펼쳤을 것이다.
134|
135|가장 빠르고, 고통 없는 죽음을 내렸을 테다.
136|
137|‘어쩌면 그걸 위해 다시 세상에 나왔을지도 모르지.’
138|
139|하지만 적천강의 목적은 이뤄지지 못했다. 조필은 옛 스승보다 한발 빨리 나를 만났고, 목숨을 잃었다.
140|
141|과연 적천강이 어떻게 반응할…….
142|
143|“빚을 졌구나.”
144|
145|“예?”
146|
147|“못 들었느냐? 네게 빚을 졌다고 했다.”
148|
149|“아뇨, 듣긴 했는데.”
150|
151|얼떨떨해서 그러지.
152|
153|이렇게 쉽게, 간단하게 저런 말이 나올 줄은 정말 꿈에도 몰랐다.
154|
155|이게 무슨 일인가 싶어 눈을 깜빡이는 내게 적천강이 말했다.
156|
157|“누군가는 그 아이를 멈춰야 했다. 십 년 전 내가 했어야 할 일을 네가 대신한 것이다. 그리고…….”
158|
159|돌연 적천강이 입술을 움찔거렸다. 마치 누군가에게 그런 말을 하는 것이 처음인 사람처럼.
160|
161|잠깐 주춤하던 그가 마침내 입을 뗐다.
162|
163|“미안하다. 일전의 섣부른 행동에 대해서 너희들 전부에게 진심으로 사과하마.”
164|
165|나도 모르게 목소리가 튀어나왔다.
166|
167|“헐.”
168|
169|“헐?”
170|
171|“아, 아닙니다. 너무 놀라서 저도 모르게 그만.”
172|
173|“노부가 사과하는 것이 그렇게 놀랄 일이냐?”
174|
175|충분히 그럴 만한 일인 것 같은데. 그리고 본인도 엄청 어색해했으면서, 뭘.
176|
177|“……어, 그게.”
178|
179|어물쩍 말꼬리를 흐리던 나는 일그러지는 적천강의 얼굴을 보고 얼른 말을 바꿨다.
180|
181|“천하에 명성이 자자하신 화왕 적천강 대협께서 저같이 한참 어린 후배에게 직접 사과까지 하시다니! 적 대협의 호쾌한 성품과 겸손함에 저절로 허리가 굽혀질 뿐입니다.”
182|
183|“…….”
184|
185|“…….”
186|
187|얼굴 표정 봐라. 지킬과 하이드의 싸움이 따로 없다.
188|
189|나를 때릴지 말지, 극심한 내면 갈등을 얼굴 근육으로 표현하던 적천강이 이내 한숨을 내쉬었다.
190|
191|“도무지 종잡을 수 없는 놈이군. 이만 물러가거라.”
192|
193|“넵.”
194|
195|“저 아이들도 모두 데려가고.”
196|
197|청풍은 탁자에 이마를 박고 쿨쿨 자는 중이고 혁무진은 여전히 마당에 엎어져 있다.
198|
199|적천강의 마음이 바뀌기 전에 잽싸게 짐덩이들을 수거한 뒤 2층으로 올라가려는데 잊고 있던 사실 하나가 떠올랐다.
200|
201|‘아, 맞다. 화염신장의 비급이랑 검은 돌려줘야 하는데.’
202|
203|열화신단은 이미 먹어 버렸으니 어쩔 수 없다지만 남은 물건들은 돌려줘야 한다.
204|
205|적천광과의 문제는 오늘 하루를 마지막으로 끝내고 싶은 마음이 간절했다.
206|
207|“저어, 적 대협. 죄송하지만 하나 더 말씀드릴 것이……”
208|
209|개미만 한 목소리와 함께 돌아선 나는 다음 순간, 곧장 멈칫했다.
210|
211|쪼르르륵.
212|
213|홀로 남겨진 적천강이 술을 따르고 있었다.
214|
215|한 잔, 그리고 두 잔. 텅 빈 맞은편 자리에 술잔을 내려놓은 그가 말없이 술을 마시기 시작했다.
216|
217|물끄러미 그 모습을 바라보다가 문득 생각했다.
218|
219|‘작네.’
220|
221|화왕(火王)이라 불리는 거인의 뒷모습은 작고 쓸쓸했고, 나는 조용히 돌아서서 계단을 올랐다.
222|
223|
224|
225|* * *
226|
227|
228|
229|등 뒤의 기척이 사라지고, 적천강이 중얼거렸다.
230|
231|“넌 죽어 마땅한 놈이다.”
232|
233|안휘성에서만 수십을 죽였다. 지난 십 년간 얼마나 많은 이들이 제자의 손에 희생되었을지 짐작도 되지 않았다.
234|

*I thought the old man had neither blood nor tears in him.*

[P8]
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.

[P9]
I had never imagined that this irascible Supreme Peak master had a past like this. I also had to revise my assessment of Jopil, whom I had dismissed as merely insane.

[P10]
*He was even crazier than I thought.*

[P11]
He had thoroughly used and discarded the Master who had saved him from the brink of death. From what I’d heard, he clearly hadn’t felt a shred of guilt, even at the very end.

[P12]
I was shocked that anyone could be filled with such pure malice—and relieved that Jopil no longer existed in this world.

[P13]
“But he still managed to escape alive. The Nangong Family must have been keeping a close eye on him.”

[P14]
The Nangong Family—a staple of martial arts novels.

[P15]
They were one of the Five Great Families, an organization said to rival the Nine Sects and One Gang. I might not know the details, but hunting down and killing a single fugitive should have been nothing to them.

[P16]
Unless someone had helped him.

[P17]
“Could it be…?”

[P18]
At my question, Jeok Cheongang calmly nodded.

[P19]
“I went to the Azure Sky Sword King and asked for his help. It was the last duty I could perform.”

[P20]
The Disciple had abandoned his Master and left, yet the Master had protected him to the very end.

[P21]
The more I heard, the more unbelievable their Master-Disciple relationship became.

[P22]
“…That’s incredible.”

[P23]
“Incredible? I raised a Slaughter Saint like him as my Disciple, then let him loose upon the world because I was blinded by personal affection. It was a foolish choice.”

[P24]
Jeok Cheongang continued with a self-deprecating laugh.

[P25]
“The Azure Sky Sword King told me the same thing. He said I would regret it. He was right. Every moment of the past ten years has been filled with regret.”

[P26]
“If you could go back to that day, what would you do?”

[P27]
His answer came without hesitation.

[P28]
“I would save him. And I would regret it all over again. Even if I were given a hundred chances, the man I was then would make the same choice every time.”

[P29]
*The man I was then?*

[P30]
That was a loaded choice of words. It also meant that the Jeok Cheongang of today was different.

[P31]
*Could it be…?*

[P32]
Perhaps those ten years had been his time to prepare.

[P33]
To prepare himself to personally kill the Disciple who might still be committing atrocities somewhere in the world.

[P34]
*If that was the case…*

[P35]
A thought flashed through my mind, and I asked carefully—very carefully.

[P36]
“Um…”

[P37]
“Speak.”

[P38]
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was low. His fathomless gaze seemed to see through everything, and my heart began to pound.

[P39]
I swallowed, then opened my mouth.

[P40]
“I know there’s something you want to ask me.”

[P41]
We hadn’t sat down face-to-face just to reminisce about the past.

[P42]
He had questions for me, and I had questions for him.

[P43]
We each had things to ask and answers to give. And I wasn’t the one holding the sword hilt.

[P44]
“I’ll answer you. Whatever you ask.”

[P45]
“…”

[P46]
Jeok Cheongang, the one holding the sword hilt, silently ran his fingers over his empty wineglass.

[P47]
The silence seemed as though it might never end. Fifteen minutes? The time it took to eat a meal? Half a shichen? I had no idea how much time passed.

[P48]
A cold wind howled outside, but whether from tension or something else, my entire body was drenched in sweat.

[P49]
At last, the long silence broke.

[P50]
“…Is he dead?”

[P51]
His voice was terribly hoarse. He was trying to sound calm, but the question held a jumble of emotions.

[P52]
When I nodded, the old man’s gray eyes trembled.

[P53]
“I see. So that’s how it ended.”

[P54]
Jeok Cheongang started to tip back his wineglass out of habit, then realized it was empty and gave a hollow laugh.

[P55]
“I suspected as much. I sensed traces of our sect in you.”

[P56]
It was because of the internal energy I had gained from the Blazing Flame Divine Pill. Just as his internal energy had led me to suspect that he was the Fire King, mine had told him the same thing.

[P57]
“Did he die peacefully?”

[P58]
“That…”

[P59]
I pictured Jopil thrashing as blood streamed from his seven apertures.

[P60]
After drawing on even his innate qi, he had fought me to the death and died with half his upper body blown away.

[P61]
When I hesitated, Jeok Cheongang waved a wrinkled hand.

[P62]
“Enough. It was my fault for asking a pointless question. What peaceful death is there in a battle between martial artists?”

[P63]
“His suffering would have been brief.”

[P64]
“A man who spent his life inflicting pain on countless others received a better death than he deserved.”

[P65]
Despite his words, his expression was bitter.

[P66]
If Jeok Cheongang had found Jopil, he would have used the finest move at his disposal.

[P67]
He would have granted him the swiftest, most painless death possible.

[P68]
*Maybe that was why he returned to the world.*

[P69]
But Jeok Cheongang had failed to achieve his goal. Jopil had encountered me before his former Master could reach him, and lost his life.

[P70]
How would Jeok Cheongang react—

[P71]
“I owe you a debt.”

[P72]
“Pardon?”

[P73]
“Did you not hear me? I said I owe you.”

[P74]
“No, I heard you. It’s just…”

[P75]
I was dumbfounded.

[P76]
Never in my wildest dreams had I expected those words to come from him so easily.

[P77]
As I blinked at him, wondering what on earth was happening, Jeok Cheongang continued.

[P78]
“Someone had to stop that child. You did in my stead what I should have done ten years ago. And…”

[P79]
Jeok Cheongang’s lips suddenly twitched, as though he had never said anything like this to anyone before.

[P80]
After a brief hesitation, he finally spoke.

[P81]
“I’m sorry. I sincerely apologize to all of you for acting so rashly before.”

[P82]
The word slipped out before I could stop it.

[P83]
“Whoa.”

[P84]
“Whoa?”

[P85]
“Ah, it’s nothing. I was so surprised that it just slipped out.”

[P86]
“Is it truly so astonishing for this old man to apologize?”

[P87]
It seemed plenty astonishing to me. Besides, he’d looked incredibly uncomfortable saying it, so what was he complaining about?

[P88]
“…Well, you see…”

[P89]
I trailed off awkwardly, then saw Jeok Cheongang’s face beginning to contort and quickly changed my tune.

[P90]
“The renowned Fire King, Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, personally apologizing to a junior as young as me! I can only bow before your magnanimity and humility.”

[P91]
“…”

[P92]
“…”

[P93]
Just look at his face. Jekyll and Hyde were fighting it out right there.

[P94]
Every muscle in Jeok Cheongang’s face conveyed his fierce inner struggle over whether or not to hit me. Eventually, he sighed.

[P95]
“I cannot make heads or tails of you. You may leave now.”

[P96]
“Yes, sir.”

[P97]
“And take those children with you.”

[P98]
Cheongpung was fast asleep with his forehead pressed against the table, while Hyuk Mujin was still sprawled facedown in the courtyard.

[P99]
Before Jeok Cheongang could change his mind, I quickly gathered up the two deadweights and headed for the second floor. Then I remembered something.

[P100]
*Oh, right. I have to return the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual and the sword.*

[P101]
I had already swallowed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, so there was nothing I could do about that, but I still needed to return the other items.

[P102]
I desperately wanted to settle everything between Jeok Cheongang and me once and for all today.

[P103]
“Um, Sir Jeok. I’m sorry, but there’s one more thing I need to tell you…”

[P104]
I turned back, my voice as tiny as an ant, then stopped short.

[P105]
Wine trickled into a glass.

[P106]
Left alone, Jeok Cheongang was pouring drinks.

[P107]
One glass, then another. He placed the second wineglass before the empty seat across from him and began drinking in silence.

[P108]
I watched him for a moment, then suddenly thought:

[P109]
*He looks small.*

[P110]
The back of the giant known as the Fire King looked small and lonely.

[P111]
I quietly turned away and climbed the stairs.

[P112]
* * *

[P113]
Once the presence behind him had disappeared, Jeok Cheongang muttered,

[P114]
“You deserved to die.”

[P115]
Jangcheon had killed dozens in Anhui alone. There was no telling how many people had fallen victim to his Disciple over the past ten years.

[P116]
“‘Might makes right,’ was it? The same applied to you. In the end, you died at the hands of someone stronger.”

[P117]
No one remained strong forever, just as no one remained weak forever.

[P118]
Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, was weaker than someone.

[P119]
Yet some people forgot that fact. Drunk on their own strength—or on blood—they strayed down the wrong path.

[P120]
“What a pathetic fool.”

[P121]
Jeok Cheongang drained his drink. His Disciple’s words from that day long ago seemed to echo in his ears.

[P122]
*I have never changed. Not once, from the day I first met you until now.*

[P123]
Over the past ten years, he had turned those words over in his mind countless times. That single sentence had lodged near his heart like a dagger and tormented him.

[P124]
“Did you truly never change? Not even once?”

[P125]
They had spent many years together. At times, Jeok Cheongang had been a strict teacher; at others, he had cared for his Disciple like a loving father.

[P126]
No—he had believed that was what he had done.

[P127]
But it had all been an illusion. If it had truly been otherwise, Jangcheon would have chosen a very different path.

[P128]
“How could rice paper be black from the beginning?”

[P129]
Being born into this world was like receiving a blank sheet of rice paper.

[P130]
A person passed through countless moments between birth and death.

[P131]
When death finally arrived, those moments came together to complete a single painting. The painting Jangcheon had created was… entirely ink-black.

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang had watched from closer than anyone, yet he had never seen it.

[P133]
“Cheon.”

[P134]
The old man stared at the seat across from him, where a wineglass had been set. One by one, phantomlike figures appeared in the empty chair.

[P135]
A child hunched over as he stuffed dumplings into his mouth. A boy clutching the wooden sword his Master had made for him, his cheeks flushed bright red.

[P136]
His limbs lengthened, and his gaze sharpened. Before long, a tall young man stood glaring at the old man.

[P137]
*Kill me.*

[P138]
That day, Jeok Cheongang had been unable to answer his Disciple’s cutting words.

[P139]
But if he ever met his Disciple again, there was something he had desperately wanted to say.

[P140]
“I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.”

[P141]
A cold wind whistled through the door of the old inn and swept across the wineglass.

[P142]
* * *

[P143]
“Benefactor!”

[P144]
I awoke to a terrible racket. Cheongpung, practically bursting with excitement, was bouncing up and down.

[P145]
“This is my pavilion, so why are you… Ah.”

[P146]
Right. This wasn’t the Jin Family of Taiyuan. It was an inn.

[P147]
At the same time, the events of the previous day flashed through my mind like a panorama. It wouldn’t have been an exaggeration to say I had crossed the boundary between life and death.

[P148]
Well, that aside—

[P149]
“Stop jumping around. There’s enough dust in here already.”

[P150]
“I’m allowed to jump today!”

[P151]
How was anyone supposed to sleep through this?

[P152]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been curled up like a shrimp in one corner of the floor, blearily opened his eyes.

[P153]
“Is this… paradise?”

[P154]
That bastard started talking nonsense the moment he woke up.

[P155]
It was absurd, but then I remembered that yesterday, after trying to escape on his own, he had been knocked unconscious by a duck bone Jeok Cheongang flicked at him.

[P156]
“You awake?”

[P157]
“Captain?”

[P158]
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened when he saw me. Then he sighed.

[P159]
“So this isn’t paradise.”

[P160]
“…What the hell is that supposed to mean, you bastard?”

[P161]
“It was a joke. A joke. I’m just glad to see you alive again.”

[P162]
“Says the guy who tried to run away on his own.”

[P163]
“Come on. Why do you have to put it like that?”

[P164]
Grinning shamelessly, Hyuk Mujin looked around. More precisely, he looked at Cheongpung, who was running laps around the room like a train.

[P165]
“What’s all this commotion so early in the morning? What happened to make him run around like that?”

[P166]
“No idea. He says he’s allowed to jump today.”

[P167]
“He must’ve eaten something tasty.”

[P168]
“…”

[P169]
It was obviously bullshit, but since we were talking about Cheongpung, its credibility skyrocketed.

[P170]
Giving him a doubtful look, I asked Cheongpung,

[P171]
“What day is it today?”

[P172]
Cheongpung, who had been circling the room and driving me crazy, stopped dead.

[P173]
“Benefactor, you don’t even know that?”

[P174]
“…Let’s refrain from saying things like that. It hits ten times harder coming from you.”

[P175]
“It’s the first day of the new year. New Year’s Day!”

[P176]
Hyuk Mujin and I nodded at the same time.

[P177]
“Ah, so it’s New Year’s Day.”

[P178]
“Right. It’s already New Year’s Day.”

[P179]
“I thought it was something els—”

[P180]
“Yeah. A whole year has already pass—”

[P181]
After a brief silence, a profound realization struck us.

[P182]
*Ah. The Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

[P183]
At that moment, Wipeng’s threat from before I left the family rang vividly in my ears.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
